stimuli.text: Researchers grew a population of flour beetles in a container with a fixed supply of resources and counted the population every two days.
Students placed potato cores of equal mass in sucrose solutions of different concentrations at 22 °C. After 24 hours, they measured each core's percent change in mass.

In liver cells, the hormone epinephrine binds a G protein-coupled receptor. The activated G protein activates adenylyl cyclase, which converts ATP to cyclic AMP (cAMP). cAMP activates protein kinase A, which starts a phosphorylation cascade that leads to the breakdown of glycogen into glucose. An enzyme in the cell breaks down cAMP.

In a population of 1000 beetles, dark fur (allele B) is dominant to light fur (allele b). Researchers count 40 beetles with light fur. Assume the population is in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium (p + q = 1; p² + 2pq + q² = 1).
Two pea plants heterozygous for height (T, tall, dominant) and flower color (P, purple, dominant) were crossed, producing 640 offspring.

questions.stem: A mutation causes a G protein to remain permanently active. What is the most likely effect?

options.why: That is unrelated.
An active G protein turns the pathway on.

options.text: The response continues even without the signal
options.why: Correct. Downstream steps stay switched on.

options.text: The cell can no longer bind the ligand
options.why: Binding is upstream of the G protein.

questions.explanation: Downstream steps stay switched on.

questions.stem: Why are genetically uniform crops vulnerable to disease?

options.why: Diverse populations are more resilient.
They can.

options.text: If one plant is susceptible, nearly all are, because they share the same alleles
options.why: Correct. Low genetic diversity reduces resilience.
Growth rate is not the issue.

questions.explanation: Low genetic diversity reduces resilience.

questions.stem: How does a phosphorylation cascade amplify a signal?

options.text: Each activated kinase activates many molecules at the next step
options.why: Correct. Each step multiplies the number of active molecules.
Phosphatases remove them.
It produces a response, not ligand.
One ligand binds one receptor.

questions.explanation: Each step multiplies the number of active molecules.

questions.stem: Which factor limits population growth in a density-dependent way?

options.why: Correct. Disease spreads faster in crowded populations.
That is density-independent.
Weather affects populations regardless of density.
That is density-independent.

questions.explanation: Disease spreads faster in crowded populations.

questions.stem: Which molecule can diffuse directly across a phospholipid bilayer most easily?

options.why: Proteins are too large.
Ions are repelled by the hydrophobic core.
Glucose is large and polar.
Correct. Small nonpolar molecules pass through the hydrophobic core.

questions.explanation: Small nonpolar molecules pass through the hydrophobic core.

questions.stem: Two cube-shaped cells have side lengths of 1 µm and 6 µm. Which statement correctly compares their surface area-to-volume ratios?

options.text: The 1 µm cell has a ratio of 6, which is greater than the 6 µm cell's 1, so it exchanges materials more efficiently
options.why: Correct. For a cube, SA:V = 6s²/s³ = 6/s.

options.text: The 6 µm cell has the greater ratio, 36, so it exchanges materials more efficiently
options.why: SA:V decreases as size increases.

options.text: Both cells have the same ratio, 6, because both are cubes
options.why: The ratio depends on side length.

options.text: The 1 µm cell has a ratio of 6, which is greater, so it exchanges materials less efficiently
options.why: A greater ratio means more surface per unit volume: more efficient exchange.

questions.explanation: SA:V = 6/s: 6 for 1 µm and 1 for 6 µm. Smaller cells have more surface area per unit volume.

questions.stem: One strand of DNA reads 5′-TTTGAAGA-3′. What is the sequence of the complementary strand, written 5′ to 3′?

options.why: DNA contains T, not U.
Correct. Pair each base and reverse the direction, because strands are antiparallel.
The complementary strand is antiparallel; written 5′ to 3′ it is reversed.
Each base must be paired, not just reversed.

questions.explanation: The complement of 5′-TTTGAAGA-3′ is 3′-AAACTTCT-5′, written 5′-TCTTCAAA-3′.

questions.stem: A PCR reaction starts with 1 copy of a target DNA sequence. Assuming each cycle doubles the DNA, how many copies are present after 30 cycles?

options.why: Correct. Each cycle doubles the number of copies.
Growth is exponential with base 2.
There are 30 doublings.
Copies double each cycle; they do not increase by 2.

questions.explanation: After 30 doublings: 1 × 2^30 copies.

questions.stem: A linear polysaccharide made of 126 glucose molecules is completely hydrolyzed. How many water molecules are consumed?

options.why: Correct. A chain of 126 monomers has 125 bonds, and each bond involves one water molecule.
There is one fewer bond than monomers in a linear chain.
There is one fewer bond than monomers.
Each bond involves one water molecule, not two.

questions.explanation: Linking 126 monomers forms 125 bonds; each is broken using one water molecule.

questions.stem: A liver cell and a nerve cell from the same person have the same DNA but make different proteins. Why?

options.why: Correct. Differential gene expression.
Their genomes are the same.

questions.explanation: Differential gene expression.

questions.stem: Why can cells divide uncontrollably when a gene for a growth-factor receptor is mutated so the receptor is always active?

options.text: The cell behaves as if it is always receiving signals to divide
options.why: Correct. A constitutively active receptor drives division without the signal.
It is always active.
It divides instead.

questions.stem: Which is the best measure of an organism's evolutionary fitness?

Strength does not define fitness.

options.why: Correct. Fitness is reproductive success.
Longevity matters only if it increases reproduction.

questions.explanation: Fitness is reproductive success.

questions.stem: Methylation of DNA in a gene's promoter usually has which effect?

parts.prompt: Describe the role of cAMP in this pathway.

parts.prompt: Explain how a single epinephrine molecule can cause the release of a large number of glucose molecules.

Expected heterozygotes.

parts.prompt: Birds that prey on the beetles find beetles with dark fur more easily on the new background. Predict how the frequency of the b allele will change over several generations, and justify your prediction.

parts.prompt: Calculate the chi-square value and determine whether to reject the null hypothesis at p = 0.05 (critical value 7.81 for 3 degrees of freedom).

rubric.criterion: Correct chi-square value.
Correct conclusion with comparison to the critical value.
